title: Sell Mineral Rights in Republic, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Republic, PA
metaDescription: Republic, Fayette County mineral rights owner? We buy oil and gas interests tied to this old coal-patch community, fair cash offers, plain answers.
heroLead: Republic is another Fayette County coal-patch community, built up around a mine that shaped the town's history long before anyone talked about Marcellus shale, and mineral ownership here often carries the same layered coal-and-gas history we see across this part of the county.
intro: Families in Republic sometimes assume their mineral rights were sold off generations ago along with the coal, and that's not always true — oil and gas rights were frequently held separately from coal, meaning you may still own something worth real money even if the coal under your property has long since been mined out.

sections.heading: Coal Was Mined Out, But Gas Rights May Remain
paragraphs: We trace the full recorded history of coal, oil, and gas severances on Republic-area parcels, since it's common to find that a coal company took the coal generations ago while oil and gas rights stayed with the family or passed through a separate chain entirely. Confirming that distinction is often the single most important part of our review.

This part of Fayette County sits on the southern flank of the wet-gas Marcellus play, and while activity here hasn't matched the density seen further north in Washington and Greene counties, tracts near active units can still carry real value.

sections.heading: A Simple Process for a Complicated History
paragraphs: Once we've confirmed what you actually hold, the rest of the process is straightforward: we make an offer based on current activity, handle the paperwork through the Fayette County recorder of deeds in Uniontown, and close once you're ready, without asking you to do the legwork yourself.

faqs.question: The coal company mined out our land decades ago. Do we still own anything?
faqs.answer: Possibly, since oil and gas rights are often held separately from coal. We check the recorded history to confirm what you still own.

faqs.question: Is there current gas activity near Republic?
faqs.answer: Activity varies by specific location within Fayette County; we check proximity to active units for your particular parcel.

faqs.question: What records do you need from me to get started?
faqs.answer: A deed or tax parcel number helps, but we can locate what's needed from the Fayette County courthouse if you don't have paperwork on hand.

faqs.question: Does it matter if the coal patch itself has been demolished?
faqs.answer: No, whether the old company houses or mine structures still stand has no bearing on your underlying mineral rights, which exist independently of surface conditions.
